title: Administration
subtitle: Users, groups, permissions, sessions, single sign-on and the cluster

users.title: Users
users.subtitle: Accounts that can sign in to the web console and call the HTTP API
users.searchPlaceholder: Search by username or display name…

form.usernameHelp: The name used to sign in. It can be changed after creation.
form.newUsernameHelp: Leave blank to keep the current username.
form.displayNameHelp: Shown in the session list and in audit entries.
form.newPasswordHelp: Leave blank to keep the current password.
form.disabledHelp: A disabled account cannot sign in, and its existing sessions are invalidated immediately.
form.totpHelp: Turning this off means the user is not asked for a code at their next sign-in.
form.totpEnableDenied: An administrator cannot turn two-factor on for someone else — only that user can enrol an authenticator from their own profile. Once they have, this switch unlocks so it can be turned off here.
form.resetTotpConfirm: Clear two-factor authentication for {name}? They can then enroll a new authenticator.
form.sessionTimeoutHelp: Set 0 to use the server default.
form.memberOfGroupsHelp: Users inherit the permissions of the groups they belong to.
form.ssoManagedGroupsHelp: When on, membership follows the identity provider's group claims and edits here have no effect.
form.passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match
form.passwordTooShort: Password must be at least {min} characters
form.cannotDisableSelf: You cannot disable the account you are signed in with
form.cannotDeleteSelf: You cannot delete the account you are signed in with

delete.title: Delete user {name}
delete.body: Delete the user {name}? All of their sessions and user-specific permissions are removed too.

sessions.title: Active sessions for {name}
sessions.empty: This user has no active sessions
sessions.revokeAllConfirm: Revoke every session belonging to {name}? They are signed out immediately.

createToken.title: Create an API token for {name}
createToken.warning: The full token is shown only once. Copy and store it now.

groups.title: Groups
groups.subtitle: Grant permissions to a set of users at once

form.name: Group name
form.membersHelp: Pick from existing users. Multiple selections are allowed.
form.noMembers: This group has no members yet

delete.title: Delete group {name}
delete.body: Delete the group {name}? Its members are unaffected, but permissions gained through the group stop applying.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.subtitle: Grant users and groups access per functional section
permissions.sectionHelp: Each section is authorized separately. Users without a grant cannot see the matching pages.
permissions.empty: No permissions granted for this section yet
permissions.emptyHint: Only users or group members holding a grant can reach this feature.
permissions.resetConfirm: This clears every grant for the section, leaving access to administrators only. Continue?
permissions.inheritNote: Zone-level permissions can be refined on each zone's Permissions tab.
permissions.selfLockoutWarning: Warning: the grants you are editing include your own account or one of your groups. Saving may immediately revoke your access to this page.

flags.canView: Can view the content of this section

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.subtitle: Every active sign-in session and API token right now
sessions.searchPlaceholder: Search by username, address or token fingerprint…
sessions.currentHint: This is the session you are using now. Revoking it signs you out immediately.
sessions.deleteConfirm: Revoke this session for {user}? That device loses access immediately.
sessions.deleteAllBody: This signs out every user and invalidates all API tokens, breaking automation immediately. Continue?
sessions.deleteAllPreservesCurrent: The session you are using right now is kept so you are not locked out of the console.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.subtitle: Sign in to the console with an OpenID Connect / OAuth2 identity provider
sso.enableHelp: Once enabled, the sign-in page shows a “Continue with single sign-on” button. Check the configuration carefully, or sign-in may fail.
sso.authorityHelp: The base address of the OIDC authorization server.
sso.clientSecretHelp: Leave blank to keep the currently stored secret.
sso.metadataAddressHelp: Optional. Defaults to /.well-known/openid-configuration derived from the authority.
sso.scopesHelp: One per line. Usually openid, profile and email.
sso.allowSignup: Create an account automatically on first sign-in
sso.allowSignupHelp: When off, only accounts that already exist can sign in through single sign-on.
sso.allowSignupOnlyForMappedUsers: Auto-create accounts only for users matched by a group map
sso.allowSignupOnlyForMappedUsersHelp: Works with the group map below to limit which identity provider groups get access.
sso.groupMapHint: Maps identity provider group names to local groups, syncing membership at sign-in.
sso.testHint: Opens the single sign-on flow in a new window so you can verify the configuration.
sso.warning: A misconfiguration can lock everyone out. Keep a local administrator account as a fallback.
sso.redirectUriHelp: Register this address in the application settings at your identity provider.

cluster.title: Cluster
cluster.subtitle: Synchronize configuration and zone data between the primary and secondary nodes

notInitialized.title: The cluster is not initialized
notInitialized.body: Once initialized, this machine becomes the cluster primary and other servers can join and sync configuration.
notInitialized.clusterDomainHelp: Used to identify and resolve nodes inside the cluster. A dedicated domain is recommended.
notInitialized.primaryNodeIpAddressesHelp: One address per line. These are the addresses other nodes use to reach this primary; prefilled with this machine's own addresses.
notInitialized.success: Cluster initialized — this machine is the primary node

nodes.title: Cluster nodes
nodes.empty: No other nodes in the cluster yet
nodes.deleteSecondaryHint: Removes the node from the cluster and deletes the configuration data on it.
nodes.deleteSecondaryConfirm: Delete the secondary node {name}? The cluster configuration on it is erased.
nodes.removeSecondaryHint: Removes it from the cluster list only; the node keeps its own data.
nodes.removeSecondaryConfirm: Remove the node {name} from the cluster? Its data is not deleted.

join.title: Join an existing cluster
join.body: Add this machine to an existing cluster as a secondary node.
join.secondaryNodeIpAddressesHelp: One address per line. The primary uses these to reach this secondary.
join.primaryNodeIpAddressHelp: Optional. Pins the primary to one address so the handshake cannot be redirected by a different DNS answer.
join.ignoreCertificateErrorsHelp: Only for a self-signed certificate on the primary. Turning this on removes any guarantee about who you are talking to.
join.credentialsHelp: Used once, to authorize this node to pull the cluster configuration. The credentials are not stored here.
join.primaryNodeTotpHelp: The primary's administrator has two-factor authentication on, so the current code is required as well.
join.success: This machine has joined the cluster

secondary.title: Secondary node actions
secondary.leaveConfirm: Make this machine leave the cluster? It stops syncing configuration from then on.
secondary.leaveSuccess: This machine has left the cluster
secondary.promoteHint: Use when the primary is permanently lost. This machine takes over the cluster.
secondary.promoteConfirm: Promote this machine to primary? Confirm the old primary really is unrecoverable, otherwise the cluster splits.
secondary.promoteSuccess: This machine is now the primary node
secondary.resyncHint: Pulls the entire configuration from the primary node again.
secondary.resyncConfirm: Resyncing overwrites this machine with the primary's configuration. Unsynced local changes are lost.
secondary.forceLeaveHelp: Needed when the primary can no longer be reached. This machine stops being a secondary without the primary confirming the removal.
secondary.forceDeletePrimaryHelp: Needed when the primary is permanently lost. Its record is dropped here so this machine can take over the cluster.
secondary.updatePrimaryHelp: Enter the new address after the primary node has moved.
secondary.updatePrimaryIpsHelp: Optional, one address per line. Pins the primary to these addresses; leave the list empty to go back to resolving it by name.

primary.title: Primary node actions
primary.titleHelp: Available because this machine is the cluster primary.
primary.setOptionsBody: How often the primary refreshes node heartbeats and pushes configuration, and how long it waits before retrying a failed attempt.

ipAddress.title: This node's cluster IP
ipAddress.hint: The addresses the cluster uses to identify this node. On a multi-homed host you may need to set them manually.

delete.title: Delete cluster
delete.body: Delete the cluster? This machine leaves it and clears its cluster configuration, and the other nodes lose their sync source.
delete.forceDeleteHelp: Needed when a secondary node can no longer be reached. The cluster is deleted here even though that node still holds a copy of the configuration.
